Here it is, 2017, and we still don't have a way to equalize loud and soft sounds from a television

Um, I hate to break it to you but many TVs from the late 90s through 2000s had this feature. Automatic Volume Control (AVC) was a feature made to equalize dramatic volume shifts in shows and commercials. It worked great for commercials that had an actual loudness higher than the program, but it made shows and especially movies sound weird. Imagine watching an action movie where there are loud and soft volume levels happening at various times in a scene. Now imagine the loud parts (like explosions) are equalized down to the dialog levels. It sounds unnatural and gets on your nerves after a while. AVC fell off the feature list for this reason as well as many people thinking it didn't work on commercials because they still seemed "loud" but really weren't due to audio frequency compression techniques that didn't change the volume level but still sounded loud. I imagine we could make a better version today but it would still have some quirks that sound wrong. But if you really want one, look into external AVC modules that can be added to audio signals for TV, stereo and other audio uses since they do exist.
